title: Mechanical Music: does the game design hold?
summary: A game-design (GDD) check for a clockwork rhythm puzzle: the mechanics drawn as schemas, then 21 design questions in 6 themed pages.
description: *Mechanical Music* is a clockwork rhythm toy: gears, cams and hammers on a pegboard turn a motor's rotation into a beat. Here's the design as I understood your notes, with the new mechanics sketched. Check I read them right, then answer the mechanics, sound and puzzle questions. Once they're in, I build the first version.

fields.label: The updated game
fields.text:
**Mechanical Music, updated with your answers**

**The game**: repair and build clockwork music machines. An input crank turns forever (one turn per bar). On a fixed pegboard you **stack** gears, belts, cams and hammers so the machine plays a rhythm, and with pitch rotators, a melody.

**Two modes**
- **Puzzles: repair the machine.** Every piece you need is already on the table. The sound pieces and the input crank are fixed (the crank only stops when something jams). Put the machine back together until it plays the target rhythm **exactly**. That match is the win; there's no score. Plus a **daily puzzle**.
- **Sandbox**: every piece on a fixed board, saved in the browser and shared by link.

**Already decided**: physical meshing; ratios via gear sizes, compound stacks, clutches and reversal; extra percussion; free orbit camera; warm workshop look; synth sounds first, samples later; **phone first**; a new project (Vite + React + three + zustand) at `mechanical-music.game.gabvdl.xyz`, public.

**Mechanics as I understood your notes** (diagrams below; correct me in the notes):
- **Stacking**: each cell is an axle. Pieces stack on it, with heights from ½ to 2. Everything that turns on one axle turns together.
- **Physical meshing**: radii must add up to one cell (12+12, 8+16, 6+18 → 1:1, 1:2, 1:3). A gap does nothing; an overlap jams. Compound stacks chain the ratios.
- **Belts** between two pulleys at the same height: same direction, ratio = pulley sizes.
- **Quarter-turn gear**: one full turn in → ¼ turn out, then it waits.
- **Cams** (rounded, wavy top) lift a **stamp hammer** that drops on the sound piece under it.
- **Rotating hammers** strike the sound pieces in their 4 neighbouring cells.
- **Clutch**: an axle piece that connects or disconnects when it is hit.
- **Sound pieces**: percussion, tuned bells, **toggles** (on/off each hit) and **pitch rotators** (each hit → next value, cycling; linked tuned pieces play that pitch).

fields.label: How does a cam drive a hammer?

options.label: **Stamp**: a vertical hammer in the cell next to the cam drops onto the sound piece stacked beneath it *(my pick)*
**Lever**: cam → lever → sound piece, three cells in a line (like the first mockup)
Both
**A real Geneva pair**: pin wheel + slotted wheel in two adjacent cells *(my pick)*
**One stack piece**: input below, intermittent output above
Both
two pulleys in the same row or column; the path must be clear at that height
**any two pulleys at the same height**; the path must be clear *(my pick)*
any two pulleys at the same height, passing over everything
**Strict**: any overlap at the same height jams, including gears, belts, hammer sweeps and diagonals *(my pick)*
**Gears only**: overlapping gears jam; hammers and belts pass through
Strict in puzzles, forgiving in the sandbox

fields.label: How tall can a stack get?

options.label: 2 cells
3 cells *(my pick)*
4 cells
Their own **sustained sound** (drone, organ pipe, music-box spring): it starts on one hit and stops on the next
A **mute switch** for the sound pieces linked to it
A **clutch**: engages or disengages an axle (song sections)
Just a light or flag (a visual cue)

fields.label: How does a pitch rotator reach the pieces it tunes?

options.label: **By touch**: it tunes the tuned pieces in its 4 neighbouring cells
**A rod you draw** from the rotator to each tuned piece *(my pick)*
**Stacked**: it tunes the piece in its own cell

fields.label: What values does a rotator hold?

options.label: **Scale degrees** in the puzzle's key, so it's always musical *(my pick)*
Any note (chromatic)
A fixed melody baked into the piece (a tiny pin barrel)

fields.label: How many positions does a rotator have?

options.label: Always 4
Always 8
2 to 8, set per piece *(my pick)*

fields.label: What does a broken machine look like at the start?

options.label: Pieces scattered in a **tray** next to the board
Pieces in the **wrong cells** on the board
Pieces **knocked over**, lying on their side
**Dusty and rusty**: they shine again once placed right
Some pieces **bolted down** as part of the puzzle
**One intended solution**: a mechanical jigsaw
**Any arrangement that plays the target exactly wins** (Opus Magnum spirit) *(my pick)*

fields.label: Must every piece end up on the board?

options.label: Yes, all of them
No: some are decoys
No rule: only the rhythm counts *(my pick)*

fields.label: How is the target rhythm shown?

options.label: **Ghost dots on the strip**, yours vs the target, live *(my pick)*
Heard only: listen and reproduce
Heard first; the strip unlocks as a hint
**Chapters** that each introduce one mechanic: gears → stacks → belts → cams → rotating hammers → quarter-turn → toggles → pitch *(my pick)*
One flat list of handmade puzzles
The daily puzzle first, plus a few tutorials
